Girindra Chandra Bonik, the predecessor of the present petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 55 of 1981 before the Subordinate Judge, Hobiganj impleading the predecessor of the present opposite parties Nos. 1-9 and other opposite parties as defendants under Order XXI, rule 103 of the Code of Civil Procedure for establishment of right and possession in the suit premises. 

 5. By his judgment dated 3st March, 1985, the learned Subordinate Judge on consideration of documentary and oral evidence adduced by the parties, decreed the suit in favour of the said Girindra Chandra Bonik on the finding that the said Mobashwar Ali failed to prove his case. 

 7. Mr. Momtaz Uddin Fakir learned advocate, appearing for the petitioners submits that Order 21 Rule 103 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not appealable and this vital point has been raised before the appellate Court but the appellate Court without adverting and considering that vital point allowed the appeal which caused serious miscarriage of justice. He next submits that learned Additional District Judge committed error in reversing the decision of the Court of 1st instance without reversing the findings recorded by it who arrived at a decision on true and proper consideration of the oral and documentary evidence. He next submits that the appellate Court failed to consider that Nandalal Roy being purchaser of the suit land by sale deed dated 8th Jaistho 1360 BS by his own money and benefit entered into agreement with the plaintiff for sale on 4-7-1962 but subsequently Nandalal resiled from his agreement and refused to execute and register deed of sale for which the plaintiff by filing Title Suit No. 13 of 1963 got decree in his favour which has been duly executed through execution case. The plea of suit property being jointly owned by Nandalal Roy and Jogendra Lal Roy have not been proved by evidence but the appellate Court failed to advert that vital aspect of the case and erroneously allowed the appeal which caused failure of justice. 

 Lal Roy and, as such, application for substitution of Sushama Bala Roy was rejected and consequent civil revision being Civil Revision No. 103 of 1968 filed before the High Court Division was also rejected. Thereafter Girindra Chandra Bonik filed Execution Case No. 10 of 1967 and got a deed of sale executed and registered and by filing title Execution Case No.8 of 1969 got delivery of possession on 30-4-1969. 

 9. It further appears that Jogendra Lal Roy, the brother of Nanda Lal Roy filed Partition Suit No. 28 of 1968 claiming joint family property with Nanda Lal Roy and the said partition suit was decreed exparte on 26-4-1968. Thereafter defendant No.1 by filing Miscellaneous Case No. 71 of 1969 under Order XXI, rules 101 of the Code of Civil Procedure prayed for restoration of possession purportedly claiming the suit land by virtue of baina patra having executed by Jogendra Lal Roy dated 7-12-1963 and after hearing the said case was allowed ordering restoration of possession. Challenging the said judgment and order, the petitioners filed Title Suit No.51 of 1981 before the Subordinate Judge, Habiganj under Order XXI, rules 103 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 10. The trial Court in his judgment held that there is no convincing evidence that Nanda Lal Roy and Jogendra Lal jointly held and possessed the suit land. The trial court with reference to DW 4 Abul Hossain, DW 5 Chunu Mia and DW 10 Shaheb Mia held that Nanda Lal resided in the suit premises till his death and defendant No.1failed to prove that on the basis of baina patra he went to the possession of the suit land on 7-12-1963. The trial court with reference to DW 1 Azizul Haque found that he himself and other persons resided in the suit land time to time. The Court also discussed the evidence of DWs 5, 6, 8, 9, 10 and 11 and held that there are anomalies in their deposition regarding possession of the suit land and that defendant No. 1 did not enter into the suit land by virtue of the baina patra dated 7-12-1963, rather the men of defendant No.1 came to the suit land after the death of Nanda Lal Roy. The trial Court also disbelieved the baina patra as claimed by defendant No. 1 and also found that Jogendra Lal Roy never claimed the suit land during the lifetime of Nanda Lal Roy. The trial Court also held that the plaintiff after getting decree in a suit for specific performance of contract got kabala through court and also obtained possession by filing execution case. The Court found that Jogendra Lal Roy filed Title Suit No. 28 of 1968 in the third Court of Munsif, Habigonj and obtained preliminary decree on 26-4-1968 impleading Nanda Lal's son Nagendra Lal Roy as defendant No.1 and Nanda Lal's daughter as defendant No. 2 although the address of defendant No.1 was shown at Habigonj town but it is claimed that his whereabouts was not known and Sushama Bala was no legal heir of Nanda Lal Roy and, as such, the decree has been obtained by practising fraud and for unknown reason Sushama Bala did not contest the suit. The trial Court by elaborate discussion also held that there is no trace that Jogendra Lal Roy and Nanda Lal Roy jointly held and possessed the suit land as member of joint family and, as such, alleged purported unregistered Batwaranama and other documents shown by defendant No.1 are nothing but collusive and created papers and accordingly the trial Court decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff upholding plaintiff's possession. 

 11. Before the Appellate Court contention was raised on behalf of the petitioner-respondent that an order passed in the proceeding under rule 103 of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure is conclusive and no appeal is maintainable against such order but the appellate Court disregarding the legal provision and established principle held that since it is a regular suit and decree is drawn thereon as such appeal is maintainable. Such view is patently illegal and not sustainable. For proper appreciation, rule 103 of Order XXI is reproduced below: 

 "Under what authority, with due respect to the learned Judges in those cases, they came to this conclusion it is difficult for me to ascertain. Section 115 does not prevent any revision on the ground that there is another remedy. Rule 103 contains the words "subject to the result of such suit, (if any)" the order passed under Rules 98, 99 and 101 will be conclusive. The word 'conclusive' means no appeal lies but it does not mean that High Court cannot revise the order of the Court passed under Rules 98, 99 and 101 of the Code of Civil Procedure." 

 13. Apart from this, right to prefer appeal is statutory right but in the instant matter rule 103 of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure mandates that order passed under the said section will be final meaning hereby that there is no scope of appeal which is clearly reiterated in 6 DLR 333. Besides jurisdiction cuts the root of the matter and if the Court got no jurisdiction everything shall fall through.
